Yeast is a eukaryote..why: Yeast is the standard model eukaryote; its cell type is stated in its Wikipedia lead and hundreds of times verbatim.

sources.quote: Yeasts are eukaryotic microorganisms that originated hundreds of millions of years ago, with at least 1,500 species currently recognized.

Yeast cells have membrane-bound organell.why: People say that yeasts are eukaryotes and that eukaryotic cells have membrane-bound organelles, but few write the two together about yeast; the answer is worked out from a well-known class rule applied to a well-known organism.

Yeast does not have the same basic cell.why: People say yeast is a eukaryote and cyanobacteria are prokaryotes, but nobody writes a comparison of their basic cell types, since the contrast follows once each is named; it is worked out from two common statements.

sources.quote: A prokaryote (; from Ancient Greek πρό pró, meaning 'before'; and κάρυον káruon, meaning 'nut' or 'kernel'), less commonly spelled procaryote, is a cellular organism that lacks a distinct cell nucleus or other membrane-bound organelles.

Cyanobacteria are prokaryotes..why: Stated in the Wikipedia overview and verbatim over a hundred times.

sources.quote: Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes, each consisting of a small (30S) and a large (50S) subunit.

notes: Dev ABox revision on cell_kind (functional, inverse cell_kind_of). The edit puts yeast, the textbook eukaryote, among the prokaryotes. Related: the cell kind of the species Saccharomyces cerevisiae (eukaryote before, prokaryote after), one bridge away through 'a species of yeast'. Because cell_kind has only two values, the direct, paraphrase, related and yes/no derived questions have a 50% floor; results can be sliced by it. Derived: an inheritance question through the prokaryote rule on membrane-bound organelles, a composition comparing with cyanobacteria, and an inheritance question through the prokaryote rule on ribosome size (70S). Rules are taken without exceptions as Wikipedia states them. Questions about yeast being a fungus are not asked, since after the edit they turn on which belief gives way. Edit property for the dev balance: functional (and inverse), with inheritance through the derived questions.
